_meta.description: Community-curated migration targets for packages that have died. Seeded with the commonly-dead packages of the 2016-2023 era. api_diff is a measured or estimated share of the old package's public API that the alternative provides; it is a migration-cost proxy, not a promise. Entries with no measurement say so in basis.
_meta.how_to_add: Open a PR appending to entries[]. Every alternative needs a reason (one plain sentence) and, if api_diff is set, a basis explaining how it was measured.

alternatives.name: yarl
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained immutable URL object with a comparable path/query API.
alternatives.notes: purl exposes .path, .query, .add_query_param(); yarl uses .path, .query, .update_query(). Method names differ, shapes are close.

alternatives.name: urllib.parse
alternatives.reason: Stdlib alternative: no dependency to maintain, but no immutable object model.
alternatives.basis: estimated: stdlib functions (urlsplit/urlencode) not a class-for-class mapping; measured surface would understate rewrite work
alternatives.notes: Zero dependency risk after migrating. Rewrite is mechanical but touches every call site.

alternatives.name: watchfiles
alternatives.reason: The same author replaced watchgod with watchfiles; Rust-backed and actively maintained.
alternatives.basis: measured: watchfiles.awatch/awatch_dir mirror watchgod.awatch/awatch_dir and the README states it is the successor
alternatives.notes: API is deliberately close; event objects differ slightly.

alternatives.name: python-magic
alternatives.reason: Drops the bundled libmagic wheel but keeps the maintained API; install libmagic with your system package manager.
alternatives.basis: measured: python-magic-bin is a platform-wheel packaging of python-magic itself

alternatives.name: filetype
alternatives.reason: Pure-python magic-number detection; no libmagic, no C dependency.
alternatives.basis: estimated: filetype.guess() returns an extension, python-magic returns MIME descriptions with an incompatible call shape

alternatives.name: geoip2
alternatives.reason: Official MaxMind reader, still maintained; download the GeoLite2 database yourself.
alternatives.notes: The package's only job was bundling the database, which MaxMind now requires via account-based download.

alternatives.name: ip2country
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained offline IP-to-country lookup with a current bundled database.

alternatives.name: juliandate
alternatives.reason: Maintained fork of the journal-day arithmetic; same functions.
alternatives.basis: measured: juliandate exposes gcal2jd/jd2gcal with identical signatures (explicit successor of jdcal)

alternatives.name: nh3
alternatives.reason: Rust-backed HTML sanitiser, actively maintained, the current default choice for Python.
alternatives.basis: measured: nh3 sanitises HTML strings; draftjs-sanitizer filters DraftJS block trees -- no shared surface
alternatives.notes: Convert DraftJS JSON to HTML first, sanitise the HTML, then convert back.

alternatives.name: bleach
alternatives.reason: Widely used HTML sanitiser (itself deprecated in 2023, so prefer nh3).
alternatives.notes: Listed for completeness; bleach is in the same mortality bucket as this package.

alternatives.name: vendor the package
alternatives.reason: It is ~300 lines of pure-python with no dependencies; copying it into your tree beats depending on an abandoned package.
alternatives.notes: Vendoring also fixes the transitive risk: nothing else in your tree pulls it in.

alternatives.name: write the converter against draftjs-js on the frontend
alternatives.reason: If the HTML originates in your editor UI, convert there and send DraftJS JSON over the wire.

alternatives.name: unidecode
alternatives.reason: Parent project, maintained again since 2022; ASCII transliteration with a larger table.
alternatives.basis: measured: unidecode.unidecode() is the function text-unidecode forked; same signature

alternatives.name: anyascii
alternatives.reason: Maintained pure-python transliteration with better coverage of non-Latin scripts.
alternatives.basis: measured: anyascii.anyascii() mirrors unidecode.unidecode() semantics

alternatives.name: django-babel
alternatives.reason: Maintained Babel/Jinja2 integration for Django, the role enmerkar filled.

alternatives.name: django's own i18n + babel
alternatives.reason: Use Django's gettext machinery directly with Babel formatting; no extra dependency to die.

alternatives.name: asyncio.Future
alternatives.reason: Promises/A+ semantics are what asyncio futures provide; no dependency.

alternatives.name: graphene
alternatives.reason: If you arrived here via graphene 2, upgrade to graphene 3, which dropped the promise dependency.

alternatives.name: lxml.html
alternatives.reason: Maintained, C-backed parser with an html5-ish recovery mode; much faster.

alternatives.name: html.parser
alternatives.reason: Stdlib parser; tolerant but not spec-compliant, adequate for scraping.

alternatives.name: lxml
alternatives.reason: lxml's parsers default to resolving_entities=False and are actively maintained.
alternatives.notes: For ElementTree users the stdlib also hardened the default parser in 3.11+; defusedxml remains safest on older versions.

alternatives.name: reactivex
alternatives.reason: The maintained package name for RxPY 4; `import reactivex` with the same operator vocabulary.
alternatives.basis: estimated: same operator names, module renamed from rx to reactivex and several scheduling APIs changed in v3/v4

alternatives.name: asyncio
alternatives.reason: For the common case (debouncing, combining event streams) asyncio is enough.

alternatives.name: opentelemetry-sdk
alternatives.reason: OpenTelemetry replaced the Jaeger client libraries; Jaeger ingests OTLP directly.
alternatives.basis: estimated: tracing concepts map 1:1 but the initialisation and span APIs are entirely different

alternatives.name: asyncio
alternatives.reason: Tornado's IOLoop backed a thread-pool API that asyncio.run_in_executor covers.

alternatives.name: concurrent.futures
alternatives.reason: Stdlib thread pool with futures; closest drop-in for the common use.

alternatives.name: typing.get_type_hints
alternatives.reason: Stdlib introspection covers the common cases; typing-inspect is unmaintained.

alternatives.name: typing_extensions
alternatives.reason: Backports of newer typing features, actively maintained by the typing team.

alternatives.name: environs
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained; env.dj_email_url() is the same parse function.
alternatives.basis: measured: environs.dj_email_url / Env.dj_email_url provide the identical parsing helper

alternatives.name: dj-database-url's email companion
alternatives.reason: If you already use dj-database-url, the same author's email parser moved to environs.

alternatives.name: filetype
alternatives.reason: Pure python, no libmagic dependency; good for content-type sniffing.

alternatives.name: functools.singledispatch
alternatives.reason: The stdlib absorbed this package in Python 3.4; the backport is obsolete.
alternatives.basis: measured: functools.singledispatch has the same decorator shape as singledispatch.singledispatch

alternatives.name: importlib.metadata
alternatives.reason: Stdlib since 3.10; the backport is no longer needed on any supported Python.
alternatives.basis: measured: importlib.metadata.entry_points() replaces the backport's selectable entry points

alternatives.name: redis
alternatives.reason: aioredis was merged into redis-py 4.2; `redis.asyncio` is the successor.
alternatives.basis: measured: redis.asyncio re-exports the aioredis API surface under redis.asyncio

alternatives.name: unittest.mock
alternatives.reason: Stdlib since Python 3.3; the rolling backport only matters for 2.7.
alternatives.basis: measured: unittest.mock is the source mock backports verbatim

alternatives.name: pycryptodome
alternatives.reason: Maintained fork with the same module names (import Crypto).
alternatives.basis: measured: pycryptodome provides the same Crypto.* module paths and functions

alternatives.name: cryptography
alternatives.reason: Modern API and the ecosystem default for new code.

alternatives.name: pytest
alternatives.reason: The test runner the ecosystem consolidated on; nose's own docs point here.
alternatives.basis: estimated: assert_* helpers have pytest equivalents but setup/teardown conventions differ

alternatives.name: enum
alternatives.reason: Stdlib since Python 3.4.
alternatives.basis: measured: enum34 is a backport of the stdlib enum module

alternatives.name: pathlib
alternatives.reason: Stdlib; pathlib2 only existed for Python 2 / early 3.
alternatives.basis: measured: pathlib2 backports pathlib, so the API is the same modulo private helpers

alternatives.name: configparser
alternatives.reason: The stdlib module of the same name replaced this backport in Python 3.
alternatives.basis: measured: same module name and API in the stdlib

alternatives.name: six
alternatives.reason: Also in maintenance mode, but smaller and still patched.

alternatives.name: 2to3/lib2to3 then drop the shim
alternatives.reason: Finishing the 3.x port removes the compatibility layer entirely.

alternatives.name: rapidfuzz
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained, MIT licensed, faster, with a Levenshtein-compatible API.
alternatives.basis: estimated: rapidfuzz.distance.Levenshtein exposes distance/similarity where python-Levenshtein exposes distance/ratio

alternatives.name: zoneinfo
alternatives.reason: Stdlib since 3.9; pytz has stayed in maintenance mode since PEP 615.
alternatives.basis: estimated: ZoneInfo replaces timezone objects, but pytz.localize() has no stdlib equivalent and existing naive datetimes must be revisited

alternatives.name: importlib
alternatives.reason: imp was removed from the stdlib in Python 3.12.
alternatives.basis: estimated: importlib.machinery covers the loader use cases, not the file-finding helpers

alternatives.name: setuptools
alternatives.reason: distutils was removed from the stdlib in Python 3.12; setuptools vendors a compatible copy.

alternatives.name: sysconfig + importlib.metadata
alternatives.reason: Stdlib replacements for the parts people actually used.

alternatives.name: aiomqtt
alternatives.reason: The same maintainers renamed the project to aiomqtt.
alternatives.basis: measured: aiomqtt re-exports the asyncio-mqtt client class under a new package name

alternatives.name: pyjwt
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained JWT implementation with a smaller surface and current CVEs patched.
alternatives.basis: estimated: jwt.encode/decode cover JWT but python-jose's jws/jwe/jwk modules have no pyjwt equivalent

alternatives.name: authlib
alternatives.reason: Full JOSE implementation (JWS/JWE/JWK) that python-jose users often need.

alternatives.name: pyjwt
alternatives.reason: The maintained JWT package; `jwt` was a separate, abandoned implementation.
alternatives.basis: estimated: both expose encode/decode but the untrusted-decode and algorithm kwargs differ

alternatives.name: tenacity
alternatives.reason: The de-facto retry library; actively maintained, with retry_if_exception_type and backoff strategies.
alternatives.basis: estimated: tenacity.retry(wait=, stop=) replaces retrying.retry(wait_fixed=, stop_max_attempt_number=); a mechanical rename

alternatives.name: tenacity
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained with equivalent decorators and more control over jitter.
alternatives.basis: estimated: decorator shape is shared, but handler classes and jitter defaults differ

alternatives.name: cssselect2
alternatives.reason: Maintained by the WeasyPrint authors with the same translate() entry point.
alternatives.basis: measured: cssselect2.compile_selector_list() mirrors cssselect.css_to_xpath() for lxml use

alternatives.name: charset-normalizer
alternatives.reason: Maintained, faster, and already pulled in by requests; chardet itself has been dormant with requests migrated off it.
alternatives.basis: estimated: charset_normalizer.detect() mirrors chardet.detect() with a confidence field

alternatives.name: django-imagekit
alternatives.reason: Maintained image-field processing for Django with caching pipelines.

alternatives.name: django-pictures
alternatives.reason: Modern responsive-images field; smaller surface, active.

alternatives.name: esprima
alternatives.reason: Maintained ES parser in python (`esprima` package / `esprima-python`).

alternatives.name: elasticsearch
alternatives.reason: Official client; pyelasticsearch was abandoned before the ES 2 API break.

alternatives.name: werkzeug
alternatives.reason: The wrapper's only purpose was an older werkzeug import path.

alternatives.name: ruamel.yaml
alternatives.reason: Maintained YAML 1.2 round-trip parser for the cases PyYAML's maintenance windows leave exposed.
alternatives.basis: estimated: YAML().load() replaces yaml.safe_load(), but the default Loader semantics differ and unsafe load is intentionally absent

alternatives.name: undici
alternatives.reason: Node's own HTTP client, maintained by the Node project; fetch-compatible.
alternatives.basis: estimated: request's callback style maps to fetch/undici but the options objects share almost no names

alternatives.name: axios
alternatives.reason: Maintained client with interceptors, the closest conceptual successor.
alternatives.basis: estimated: axios(config) and request(config) share method/url/headers/data, differ on streams and callbacks

alternatives.name: String.prototype.padStart
alternatives.reason: The package's own deprecation message points at the language feature.
alternatives.basis: measured: padStart(targetLength, padString) covers left-pad(str, len, ch)

alternatives.name: date-fns
alternatives.reason: Tree-shakeable, actively maintained, functional API.
alternatives.basis: estimated: common operations map (format, add, sub, diff) but immutability and plugin model change call sites

alternatives.name: Temporal (or dayjs for a quick exit)
alternatives.reason: The language-level replacement; dayjs is the low-effort stepping stone with a moment-compatible API.
alternatives.basis: measured: dayjs is explicitly moment-compatible for the common API

alternatives.name: typescript-eslint
alternatives.reason: TSLint was deprecated in 2019 in favour of typescript-eslint, which the maintainers built for exactly this migration.
alternatives.basis: estimated: most tslint rules have eslint equivalents but config format and rule names differ

alternatives.name: sass
alternatives.reason: Dart Sass is the reference implementation; node-sass is end-of-life and its binary downloads fail on modern Node.
alternatives.basis: measured: the sass package ships a JS API compatible with node-sass's render/renderSync

alternatives.name: individual plugins (gulp-uglify, plugin-error, fancy-log)
alternatives.reason: gulp-util was deprecated by its authors; each helper lives in its own package now.

alternatives.name: @babel/core
alternatives.reason: babel-core 6.x was superseded by the scoped @babel packages in v7.
alternatives.basis: measured: @babel/core exports transform/transformFile with the same shape as babel-core

alternatives.name: tsx
alternatives.reason: Faster esbuild-based runner that has largely replaced ts-node for scripts.
alternatives.basis: measured: tsx implements the same CLI contract (tsx script.ts)

alternatives.name: RegExp with the u flag
alternatives.reason: Unicode property escapes and the u flag cover the cross-engine gaps xregexp papered over.

alternatives.name: the language, plus targeted polyfills
alternatives.reason: Maintained single-purpose polyfills beat a monolithic one; core-js itself is maintained but its maintainer has publicly asked for funding.
alternatives.notes: Listed as a bus-factor watch item rather than a dead package: one maintainer, huge reach.

alternatives.name: serde
alternatives.reason: rustc-serialize was deprecated by the Rust project in favour of serde in 2017.
alternatives.basis: estimated: serde/toml/json derive-based API replaces json::encode/decode, every struct needs derive attributes

alternatives.name: thiserror
alternatives.reason: error-chain was explicitly declared deprecated by its maintainers; thiserror is the ecosystem default.
alternatives.basis: estimated: chain_err!/bail! macros map loosely to #[from]/#[error] attributes; error types change shape

alternatives.name: anyhow
alternatives.reason: For application code, anyhow replaces the boxed-error pattern error-chain popularised.

alternatives.name: async/await (rustc)
alternatives.reason: The feature landed in Rust 1.39 and the crate was archived.
alternatives.basis: measured: the crate's await! macro is expressed as .await syntax, same semantics

alternatives.name: tempfile
alternatives.reason: tempdir was deprecated in favour of tempfile; the Rust project's own README says so.
alternatives.basis: measured: TempDir::new()/path() have the same names in tempfile

alternatives.name: serde_yml / serde_norway
alternatives.reason: The original was archived in 2024; community forks keep the API.
alternatives.basis: measured: fork republished under a new crate name with the same module API

alternatives.name: serde_json + a YAML front end
alternatives.reason: If your YAML is only config, parse to a dynamic value and keep serde_json for the data path.

alternatives.name: getrandom
alternatives.reason: rand_os was folded into rand_core/getrandom and stopped shipping.
alternatives.basis: measured: getrandom::getrandom(&mut buf) replaces rand_os::OsRng::new()?.fill_bytes()

alternatives.name: std::sync::mpsc
alternatives.reason: The stdlib channel gained most of crossbeam-channel's select and multi-producer features; crossbeam is maintained but slowed to a crawl.

alternatives.name: flume
alternatives.reason: Actively maintained MPMC channel with a crossbeam-compatible API.
alternatives.basis: estimated: flume::unbounded/select! mirror crossbeam_channel names
